newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran denies involvement in Iraqi Kurdish fighting.
newsitem.headline: Iran denies involvement in Iraqi Kurdish fighting.

text.p: Iran on Monday denied it had helped the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) retake Sulaimaniya, Iraq's biggest Kurdish city, from a rival group.

Foreign ministry spokesman Mahmoud Mohammadi, quoted by Tehran radio, denied the charges by Massoud Barzani, leader of the Baghdad-backed Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) that Iranian troops were helping PUK forces.

Mohammadi said the charges were raised as a reaction to "protests by international bodies because of the collaboration of Barzani with the Iraqi army in suppressing the defenceless Kurdish people and turning them into refugees".
Barzani on Sunday accused Iranian forces of helping the PUK retake the key city and called for international aid against "Iran's brutal invasion".
U.N. officials and guards in Iraqi Kurdistan said on Monday that PUK forces had regained control of most of the territory they lost to the KDP six weeks ago.
Iran has repeatedly denied backing the PUK.
Baghdad has said its intrusion in Kurdish northern Iraq in late August, which helped the KDP capture the Kurdish capital Arbil, was aimed at backing the KDP against the PUK and Iran.
Tehran has said its occasional intrusions into northern Iraq, such as an attack in July, targeted Iranian Kurdish rebels based there.
